findings:
The revised plan fixes all 13 problems from the first review. The reviewer re-ran every number and confirmed it, including enemies steering clear of mines, the zig-zag spacing, the warning times, the boost tank no longer being wasted, and the hub spacing. The revision does expose two new blocking problems, and both are quick plan edits. First, the Mine Layer starts laying wherever it happens to arrive. When it arrives from the side, its mine line comes out crooked, and the plan's own "flies sideways along its line" tests would fail. It needs a short straight run-in before it starts laying. Second, the Mine Layer's first task needs three mine types that later tasks create, but it is scheduled to run alongside them. It must wait for them. Nine smaller corrections follow: test setup details, two formulas, a speed rule for the disrupted boost, and task sizing. I recommend one more re-plan to fold these in. No redesign is needed.

Simulated: at most 33° and 23 px. | t11 |

### 1. No straight run-in before laying (blocking)
APPROACH seeks the start point S, and LAY begins wherever the ship arrives. The reviewer simulated pure pursuit with the mover's 420 px/s² acceleration limit:
- arriving at 45° gives a heading 44–49° off the axis;
- arriving side-on gives 89° off the axis and up to 73 px off the path.

So the "sideways" and "on its path" rows cannot pass as specified. Add a run-in point R = S − u·150, fly R → S along the axis, and start laying (and measuring) at S. Measured with the run-in: at most 33° and 23 px, even from a side-on arrival.

### 2. Shell task needs mines from later tasks (blocking)
The Mine Layer shell (t10) builds pools for HOMING, CHAIN and PULSE. It also asserts "pulse mine keeps damage 8 after the drop" and "an empty chain pool falls back to proximity". Those scenes come from t3, t4 and t6, but t10 depends only on t2, and §3 says t10 can run with t3–t9. Fixes:
- set t10's `dependsOn` to `["t6"]` (t6 already sits after t3 and t4);
- change §3 to "t10 with t7–t9";
- reduce t11's dependencies to `["t10"]`.

### 3. Pass spacing against a standing player (minor)
A 40° rotation of the pass centre at 320 px moves it about 219 px, not the required 380 px. Rotate by the angle that achieves the spacing. Test a standing and a moving player. Skip the spacing assertion when the plan's own "proceed anyway" fallback was used.

### 4. Fixture enemy hurtbox has no shape (minor)
`fixture_enemy.tscn` lines 26–29 define a bare HurtBox area, so "placed mine is set off by an enemy" can never pass. State that those rows add a 14 px `CircleShape2D`.

### 5. Minefield clearance radius in the hub check (minor)
The planned `_element_radius()` for `Minefield` uses 280 px. With drifting mines weighted in, the real reach is radius + 120 px leash, plus the trigger radius. `Minefield` has no `trigger_radius`, so take it from the proximity mine scene. The hub layout still clears with this radius (586 / 775 px).

### 6. Child-first ready order for hand-placed mines (minor)
AUTHORED mines run `_ready()` and launch before the parent `Minefield` sets `placed` and the hostility. Require those exports to be authored on the mine, or move the placed setup into the deferred launch.

### 7. Disrupted boost slower than cruise (minor)
Scaling the whole Boost Drive and dash speed by 0.4 gives 200 px/s against 420 px/s cruise, and 140 px/s against a 180 px/s move speed. Scale only the excess over cruise, as the Shift boost does, or record the slowdown as intended.

### 8. Ambiguous test rows (minor)
- The real-mover avoidance row: fix it as head-on, because a 60 px lateral offset gives 156 < 160.
- The layer's "stays clear of earlier mines" row: exclude the pass it is breaking away from (about 61 px away when laying ends) and its own tail-drop mines.

### 9. Three inaccurate statements (minor)
- "Never sent home mid-fight": with the lead distance, a player cruising at 420 px/s is about 1587 px away, beyond the 1500 px lose radius. Restate it for players at 220 px/s or less.
- The persistence row: teleport the player stub beyond the lose radius, because the layer follows a player who flies away.
- The exit probe enters the exit phase with no planned pass. State that the exit then follows the current heading.

### 10. Fallbacks only cover level-1 gates (minor)
Registering Bomber mines as hazards could also redden rows in `test_bomber.gd` or `test_enemy_ordnance.gd`. Extend the two pre-approved levers to any existing row that fails for that reason.

### 11. Close-out task underrated (minor)
The docs, roster and as-built close-out task (t16) carries the dossier and the DECISIONS as-built section. Rate it medium, as in phase 6.
